messages.subject: Random samples of concordance lines
messages.body_plain:
What would be the most efficient way to get an exact number of random hits in a concordance?

What I'm looking at here are very high frequency words (and their full lemmas) in the BNC, so storing every hit in memory before thinning them out would be very taxing.

There are several ways to get the random selection, but they all seem to boil down to variations of one of these methods:

Situation A: Get all the hits, then randomly thin them out. Considering that searches of large corpora in which there are a large number of instances of the search token can be time-consuming, time is wasted on finding results you're never going to see. (I could live with this if it was one search, but I have to do close to 100 such searches.)

Situation B: As R finds each hit, it randomly decides whether to add it to the results pool. For this to work, you have to know how many total hits there are (if you need a specific number, as I do). Wordsmith does (or at least did) this, and it drove me crazy. Plus, you're not guaranteed to get the exact number.

Is there another way to go about this, or do I simply have to chose between A and B?

--
Kevin Parent, Ph.D, ACS, ALB
Korea Maritime University
Lt Governor of Education & Training, Korea Territorial Council (Toastmasters)
Schoolmasters: http://grou.ps/schoolmasters/
National Korea Toastmasters: http://grou.ps/koreatoastmasters

messages.subject_clean: [CorpLing with R] Random samples of concordance lines
messages.body_plain:
Off the top of my head, I might do this:

# step 1
counter <- integer(length=length(corpus.files))
for (i in seq(length(files))) {
   load each file
   find number of matches in file
   store that number in counter[i]
}

# now one knows for each file how many matches it contains (and how
many you can/want to sample)

# step 2
collector <- character()
for (i in seq(length(files))) {
   load each file
   find all matches in file
   retrieves the desired sample (e.g., ceiling(counter[i]/10)
   stores it in collector
}

STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries
